title: Event contract and timezone-aware windowing for cross-region console metrics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Console backend events (invocations, routes, user-actions) are ingested from multiple regions with different client timezones. Current upstream ingestion normalizes timestamps to UTC but we lose reliable local-time windowing semantics needed for daily/weekly business metrics (billing local-day, regional SLAs). We also need a stable event contract to support incremental materialized views and avoid expensive full-table backfills whenever a minor field is added.

Objective: Establish a formal event contract + a timezone-aware windowing strategy and landing table design that enables low-latency incremental curations for Console analytics. Deliver a migration plan (merge-on-read/upsert) that supports schema evolution, deterministic deduplication, and region-aware partitioning to reduce query cost and meet freshness SLOs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace the real-time streaming pipeline, nor does it cover UI surface changes in Console dashboards (those are follow-ups). It also does not include a full rewrite of the ingestion stack — only the landing/curated layer and materialized view logic.
acceptance_criteria:
- Event contract published (Confluence link included) with stable required fields and optional extension fields.
- Landing table (events_l0) DDL implemented with timezone-explicit timestamp and event_signature for dedupe.
- A merge-on-read ETL job that performs idempotent upserts and completes within the freshness SLO for a single region (<= 60s for warm path).
- Sample curated materialized view (curated_console_daily) producing correct local-day counts for 3 regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-sg) on a backfill test.
- Backfill plan validated on a 7-day historical window and cost estimate documented.
- Data consumers (Console billing job, SLA exporter) have integration test hooks and smoke queries passing on staging.
proposed_tables: events_l0: landing (merge-on-read) table with raw_payload (JSON), event_received_utc TIMESTAMP, event_local_ts TIMESTAMP, event_local_tz STRING, region STRING, tenant_id STRING, route_id STRING, model_variant STRING, event_type STRING, event_signature STRING, ingestion_id UUID, _metadata_version INT

events_l1_canonical: normalized event table with exploded structured fields, canonical_event_ts TIMESTAMP (UTC), local_date DATE (derived from event_local_ts and event_local_tz), partitioned by region,event_date, clustered by tenant_id

curated_console_daily: materialized daily rollup with dimensions [tenant_id, route_id, local_date, region, model_variant] and measures [invocations, tokens_in, tokens_out, avg_latency_ms, distinct_users], retention: 13 months (hot 30d), cold in cheaper storage
ddl_examples: CREATE TABLE events_l0 (ingestion_id STRING, event_received_utc TIMESTAMP, event_local_ts TIMESTAMP, event_local_tz STRING, region STRING, tenant_id STRING, route_id STRING, model_variant STRING, event_type STRING, raw_payload STRING, event_signature STRING, _metadata_version INT) PARTITION BY DATE(event_received_utc) CLUSTER BY tenant_id;
-- canonicalization job computes canonical_event_ts = to_utc(event_local_ts, event_local_tz) and local_date = CAST(event_local_ts AT TIME ZONE event_local_tz AS DATE);

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW curated_console_daily AS SELECT tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, region, local_date, COUNT(*) AS invocations, APPROX_DISTINCT(user_id) AS distinct_users, SUM(tokens_in) AS tokens_in, SUM(tokens_out) AS tokens_out, AVG(latency_ms) AS avg_latency_ms FROM events_l1_canonical WHERE event_type = 'invocation' GROUP BY tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, region, local_date;
deduplication_strategy: deterministic event_signature (sha256 of tenant_id|route_id|event_local_ts|request_id|model_variant) generated at ingestion + ingestion_id ordering. Merge-on-read upsert prefers record with highest _metadata_version and latest ingestion_id to cover late-arriving corrections. To avoid full-shuffle de-dupes in daily backfill we will maintain a small bloom_index per partition to filter likely-duplicates early (probabilistic).
schema_evolution_plan: Use an _metadata_version integer plus an extensions JSON column for optional fields. New top-level required fields must be approved via the event-contract doc. Backward-compatible additive fields are written to extensions and promoted to top-level in a controlled release with tests. A one-off job will migrate high-value promoted fields for the last 90 days before changing consumer queries.
partitioning_and_cost_controls: Partition landing by ingestion_date (UTC) and region; canonical by local_date and region. Cluster by tenant_id and model_variant. Use compact column sets for hot partitions (last 30 days) and reduce retention for verbose raw_payload in event_l0 (90 days) with cheaper snapshot-based archives after that. Documented cost delta estimated: +12% storage for timezone bookkeeping, -20% query egress on common business queries due to better partition pruning.
migration_plan: 1) Publish event-contract and obtain signoff from data owners. 2) Deploy events_l0 DDL and add ingestion instrumentation (sha256 signer). 3) Run shadow canonicalization job in staging for two weeks. 4) Run a 7-day backfill to populate events_l1_canonical; validate with reconciliation queries (counts by tenant/route/local_date). 5) Enable merge-on-read job in gradual rollout (single region -> three regions). 6) Switch Console consumers to curated_console_daily with a canary tenant. 7) Retire duplicate legacy pipelines after 2 weeks of monitoring.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for signature generation and timezone conversion library with edge cases (DST transitions, leap seconds).
- Integration tests comparing old vs. new daily counts for sampled tenants.
- Backfill run against snapshot of 30 days in staging with automated reconciliation checks.
- Load test of merge-on-read job to verify completion under peak daily throughput (simulate 50k events/s ingress for a region).
- Monitoring: daily reconciliation dashboards, freshness SLO dashboard (target P50 < 30s, P95 < 120s), and alerting on mismatched counts > 0.5%.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: DST/local-date mis-mapping causing billing mismatches. Mitigation: exhaustive DST test vectors and known-correct timezone database pinned to a release.
- Risk: Bloom filter false positives cause missed dedupe. Mitigation: tune false positive rate and keep fallback dedupe in merge stage.
- Risk: Backfill cost spike. Mitigation: limit backfill concurrency, precompute candidate partitions, and use snapshot scanning with predicate pushdown.
